passage: Irfan, you asked why I went quiet about that night, so here it is. I'm Abhinav, and we were on the bench outside the bakery after cricket, near eleven, when a jeep stopped. The officer started shouting: "Out this late? You'll spend the night in the lockup!" My knees were shaking. Then a paper was pushed at me. "Sign and you can go." I didn't read it. I said, "Sir, I'd like my father to be here first." My voice cracked, but I said it twice. The officer grumbled, but let me call. Papa came, we went home, and nothing was signed. What stayed with me was this: being scared that night didn't mean I had done anything wrong.

qa.q: Where were the friends sitting when the jeep stopped?
qa.a: They were on the bench outside the bakery after cricket.

qa.q: What was Abhinav feeling that night, and what did Abhinav take from it afterwards?
qa.a: Abhinav was scared, with shaking knees and a cracking voice, and later understood that being scared did not mean being guilty. 🤍

qa.q: What helped Abhinav most in that moment, and why?
qa.a: Staying respectful but asking for Papa before signing; it stopped Abhinav from putting a name to a paper that was never read.

qa.q: How might Papa have seen that night?
qa.a: Probably with worry, since Papa came to the scene; Abhinav does not say more, so the rest is a guess.

grounding: An officer shouts and threatens Abhinav for being out late; Abhinav stays respectful, signs nothing and asks for a parent, learning fear is not guilt.

passage:
"What are you doing here at eleven at night?" the officer shouted, torch in their faces. "Drinking? Smoking? I'll put all of you inside!"

Zubin's knees felt weak. Beside him, Rekha was shaking.

"No, sir," Zubin said, keeping his voice steady. "We were at Rekha's birthday. We're walking home."

"Birthday!" The officer slapped a notepad on the bonnet of the jeep. "Write it here. 'We were drinking at the lake.' Sign it, and I'll let you go."

"Sir, we weren't drinking. I'm not going to write that."

"You're arguing with me?"

"No, sir. I'm sorry if we worried you. But I won't sign anything. Can I please call my father? He can come right now."

The officer glared. Rekha whispered, "Just do what he says." Zubin shook his head slightly.

The officer's partner stepped in. "Let him call."

Twenty minutes later, Zubin's father arrived. The officers let them go with a warning. Zubin's hands didn't stop trembling till he got home.

qa.q: What did the officer want Zubin to write?
qa.a: He wanted Zubin to write, "We were drinking at the lake."

qa.q: What does Zubin's trembling suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: It suggests Zubin was very frightened the whole time, even though he spoke steadily, and that fear is normal, not a sign of guilt.

qa.q: Which choices by Zubin were wise, and why?
qa.a: Zubin stayed respectful, refused to sign a false statement and asked to call his father, which protected everyone without escalating things.

qa.q: Why might Rekha have wanted to do whatever the officer said?
qa.a: Rekha was shaking and scared, and may have felt that obeying would end the frightening moment faster, even if it meant signing something untrue.

grounding: It shows a teen shouted at and threatened by an officer for being out late with friends, who stays respectful, refuses to sign a confession and asks for a parent.

passage:
Last Diwali break, my cousin Alka and I were walking back from the late show when a police van stopped beside us. I'm Akash, sixteen then, and I'd never been shouted at by a stranger like that.

"What are you two doing at midnight? Running away? I'll call your school and your family and see how they like it!"

My whole body went cold. I felt guilty, even though we'd done nothing except watch a film.

The officer pushed a paper at me. "Write your details and sign that you were loitering." I remember the word loitering.

I said, "Sir, I'll tell you my name and address. I don't want to sign anything. Please let me call my father." My voice cracked on "father."

He shouted some more. I kept saying the same thing, politely. Finally he let me call. Papa came in fifteen minutes.

Afterwards Papa said, "Beta, being scared doesn't mean you did something wrong. You did right." I still think of that.

qa.q: What word does Akash remember from the paper?
Why did Akash feel guilty even though nothing wrong had happened?
qa.a: Akash felt frightened and cold all over from being shouted at, and that fear felt like guilt, even though they had only watched a film.

qa.q: What did Akash do that was wise, and why?
qa.a: Akash gave his name and address, politely refused to sign, and kept asking to call his father, which stayed respectful without admitting to something false.

qa.q: What was it like for Alka during the stop?
qa.a: Alka was probably scared too, standing beside Akash while the officer shouted and threatened to call their families.

grounding: It shows a teen shouted at and threatened by an officer for being out late, who stays respectful, does not sign anything and asks for a parent, learning that fear is not guilt.
